scams.name: Rio Galeão Airport (GIG) & Santos Dumont (SDU) Taxi Mafia & Late-Night Uber Confusion
scams.description: Rio's two airports — GIG (international, 20 km north of the city) and SDU (domestic, downtown waterfront) — host one of South America's most-documented 2025 taxi-overcharge ecosystems, with late-night arrivals especially targeted. Community reports from 2024–2025 cover GIG transport for foreigners, late-night Uber safety to Copacabana, Rio newbie tips, and tourist insights. The 2025 scams: (a) 'authorised cooperative' kiosks (Transcoopass, Special Coop, Cootramo) inside arrivals quote R$ 280–R$ 450 to Copacabana / Ipanema (real Uber R$ 90–R$ 160; real metered yellow taxi R$ 130–R$ 180); (b) sign-holders at the arrivals exit posing as 'hotel transfer' agents intercepting tourists whose hotels do NOT include shuttle; (c) Uber driver cancel-and-recontract scam — driver accepts the in-app ride, cancels at the kerb, then quotes cash R$ 200+; (d) 'meter broken' yellow taxi demands at hotel arrival with R$ 250+ flat-rate cash demand; (e) GIG-to-SDU 'connecting transfer R$ 350' sold by touts (real Uber R$ 60–R$ 100 for the 25-km ride); (f) credit-card cloning at unofficial taxi-cooperative counters via 'manual entry' card-machines. For travellers: (1) book Uber, 99 (Brazilian rideshare), or Cabify on airport Wi-Fi AFTER luggage — typical GIG to Zona Sul (Copacabana / Ipanema / Leblon) R$ 90–R$ 160, 30–45 min depending on traffic; meet driver at the designated 'Aplicativos' (apps) pickup zone signposted near each terminal exit; (2) alternatively use the OFFICIAL Premium Auto Onibus 'BRT Transolímpica' bus or 'Frescão' (Real Auto Onibus 2018) airport-to-Zona Sul service at R$ 27 per person (90 min, daytime safest option); (3) IGNORE every 'authorised cooperative' kiosk inside the terminal quoting above R$ 200; (4) for SDU domestic arrivals, Uber is even cheaper — R$ 25–R$ 60 to Zona Sul; (5) NEVER hand a credit card to any taxi driver — pay in-app or cash only; (6) for late-night arrivals (post-22:00), Uber Comfort or Uber Black is worth the R$ 30–R$ 50 surcharge for vetted drivers; (7) save Polícia Turística Rio (DEAT) +55 21 2334 6802 (English available, Av. Afrânio de Melo Franco 159, Leblon) and US Consulate Rio +55 21 3823 2000.
scams.avoidance: Book Uber/99/Cabify on airport Wi-Fi: GIG-Zona Sul R$ 90–R$ 160 Meet driver at 'Aplicativos' signposted pickup zone; SDU R$ 25–R$ 60 OR Premium / Frescão airport bus R$ 27 per person (90 min) NEVER hand credit card to any taxi driver Late-night: Uber Comfort/Black R$ 30–R$ 50 surcharge for vetted drivers
scams.location: Galeão–Antônio Carlos Jobim International Airport (GIG, Terminals 1 & 2), Santos Dumont Airport (SDU) downtown, 'Special Coop' / 'Transcoopass' kiosks, late-night arrivals corridor

scams.name: Rio Caipirinha Bar 'R$ 10,000 Bill' Honeypot Scam in Lapa & Copacabana
scams.description: Lapa and Copacabana bars host Rio's most-documented 2026 'caipirinha bill' honeypot scam — a friendly local invites the tourist to a specific bar, two caipirinhas arrive, and the bill comes back at R$ 10,000+ with bouncers blocking the door. A 2026 first-person account titled 'Esses caras tentaram golpe de R$10.000 por 2 caipirinhas' documents a near-loss of R$ 10,000 for two cocktails. A 2025 account titled 'I was scammed R$10000 in Rio de Janeiro and Bank of' documents the same pattern with a successful card-charge. Another 2025 Ipanema variant saw a R$ 27,000 loss, and 2026 community threads continue to warn of Copacabana scammers. The 2026 scam pattern: (a) friendly English-speaking local at Copacabana boardwalk or Lapa bar street invites tourist to 'best caipirinha bar nearby'; (b) walked 5–15 min to an unmarked bar (often upstairs, often a 'private room' with 'friends'); (c) 2 caipirinhas + perhaps light food arrive; (d) bill: R$ 4,000–R$ 27,000 for 'premium import cachaça', 'VIP table fee', 'live music charge', 'private hostess service'; (e) bouncers block the door until card is processed; (f) some venues threaten 'we call police' if the tourist refuses (police rarely called — extortion bluff); (g) the 'friend' who brought you in receives 30–50% commission on the inflated bill. Solo male tourists from Tinder/Bumble/Badoo dates are specifically targeted in this Rio variant — same template as Jakarta Blok M and Bangkok scams. For travellers: (1) NEVER let a stranger walk you to a 'best bar nearby' — this is the consistent opening of the scam; pick venues YOURSELF from Google 4.5+ ratings (reputable Lapa: Rio Scenarium, Carioca da Gema, Bar do Mineiro in Santa Teresa); (2) ALWAYS ask for the written menu BEFORE ordering and photograph each page; verify caipirinha is R$ 18–R$ 45 (anything above R$ 80 is scam-tier); (3) refuse any 'hostess' joining your table uninvited; (4) if a bill arrives with surprise charges, pay with credit card ONLY and immediately dispute via your bank — bank will reverse charges with photographed menu; (5) for solo travellers using dating apps, YOU pick the venue, never the date — and inform your hotel of your whereabouts; (6) save Polícia Turística (DEAT) Leblon +55 21 2334 6802 (English available, 24/7 hotline); (7) US Consulate Rio +55 21 3823 2000 if extorted; (8) the 2026 case study titled 'Esses caras tentaram golpe de R$10.000' is must-read community reading.
scams.avoidance: NEVER let a stranger walk you to a 'best bar' — pick venue yourself Reputable Lapa: Rio Scenarium, Carioca da Gema, Bar do Mineiro Photograph menu BEFORE ordering; verify caipirinha R$ 18–R$ 45 Refuse hostess; pay with credit card ONLY and dispute via bank Polícia Turística DEAT +55 21 2334 6802 (24/7 English)
scams.location: Lapa nightlife district (Avenida Mem de Sá, Rua do Lavradio), Copacabana boardwalk bars, Ipanema late-night street-bars, 'friendly local' guided pub crawls

scams.name: Copacabana / Ipanema Beach Pickpocket & 'Arrastão' Sweep Theft Ring
scams.description: Rio's beaches host South America's most-documented 2025 beach-theft ecosystem — both single-target pickpocketing and the infamous 'arrastão' (sweep theft) where a coordinated 10-30-person crew sweeps a section of beach, snatching anything not anchored. Community reports from 2025 cover Rio tourist tips, newbie advice, first-person 'I got ripped off' stories, petty-theft cross-region discussions, and the broader 2025 safety baseline. The 2025 scams: (a) phone-snatch from beach towels — child or teen runs past, grabs phone, hands off to scooter accomplice on Avenida Atlântica; (b) 'arrastão' beach sweep — most documented at Copacabana Posto 2–4 and Ipanema Posto 9 on weekend afternoons / public holidays / Carnaval; coordinated group ages 14–25 sprints through a section grabbing phones, bags, sunglasses, flip-flops; (c) distraction-team: one person 'falls' or 'spills drink', partner lifts wallet/phone; (d) beach-kiosk (quiosque) drink-spike at evening hours targeting solo tourists; (e) snorkel/sarong vendor 'free henna tattoo' that becomes R$ 150 demand; (f) 'beach umbrella + chair rental R$ 100' from unauthorised vendor (real R$ 30–R$ 50 from quiosque); (g) Avenida Atlântica boardwalk evening pickpocketing at outdoor café tables. For travellers: (1) bring NOTHING to the beach you cannot afford to lose — phone, wallet, watch, jewellery stay in the hotel safe; carry only beach-tote with sunscreen, towel, R$ 50 cash, and a single basic card you don't mind cancelling; (2) use a quiosque (kiosk) chair-and-umbrella rental at R$ 30–R$ 50 — staff will keep an eye on your minimal belongings while you swim; (3) NEVER leave anything on the towel while you swim — 'it'll be fine for 5 min' is exactly when arrastão sweeps; (4) for evening beach walks, stick to the well-lit Avenida Atlântica side, not the sand after dusk; (5) refuse every 'free henna tattoo / sarong / massage' beach vendor; firm 'não obrigado'; (6) at outdoor café tables, keep phone in zipped bag, never on table; (7) for Carnaval / NYE / Réveillon, the arrastão risk is elevated 5–10× — leave valuables at hotel and use crossbody bag with zipper; (8) Polícia Turística (DEAT) for theft: +55 21 2334 6802; file a Boletim de Ocorrência (BO) within 24 hours for insurance claims.
scams.avoidance: Bring NOTHING to the beach you can't afford to lose Use quiosque chair-and-umbrella R$ 30–R$ 50; staff watches belongings NEVER leave items on towel while swimming Carnaval / NYE: arrastão risk 5–10×; valuables in hotel safe DEAT Tourist Police +55 21 2334 6802; BO within 24 hours
scams.location: Copacabana beach (Posto 2–6 zones), Ipanema beach (Posto 8–10 zones), Leblon beach, beach kiosks (quiosques), Avenida Atlântica boardwalk evenings

scams.name: Christ Redeemer & Sugarloaf 'Skip-the-Line VIP' Tour Operator Fraud
scams.description: Rio's two iconic monuments — Christ the Redeemer (Cristo Redentor on Corcovado mountain) and Sugarloaf (Pão de Açúcar) cable car — are universal Rio bucket-list items, and the 2025 third-party reseller ecosystem exploits ticket-routing complexity. Community reports document the legitimate Sugarloaf booking process, a specific 2025 warning titled 'DO NOT TOUR WITH OLAFEMI TOURS' about a named operator, and broader tour-operator selection tips. Legitimate ticketing: Christ the Redeemer via the official Trem do Corcovado train (paineirascorcovado.com.br) is R$ 105 weekday / R$ 116 weekend round-trip foreigner; via Paineiras Shuttle Vans (paineirascorcovado.com.br) is R$ 35 + R$ 33 entry = R$ 68 round-trip. Sugarloaf cable car (bondinho.com.br) is R$ 140 for foreigners (round-trip both Urca Hill + Sugarloaf summit). Both sell out 1–2 weeks ahead in high season — book DIRECT. The 2025 scams: (a) 'skip-the-line Christ Redeemer VIP tour US$ 80–US$ 150 per person' resold via Viator/GetYourGuide third parties — that's 3–6× the official R$ 116 train ticket; the 'skip-the-line' is fictional (the train has assigned departure times, no queue to skip); (b) 'private Christ Redeemer + Sugarloaf combo US$ 200 per person' bundles padding 4× DIY cost; (c) hotel concierge 'recommended tour operator' kickbacks at 1.5–2× direct rate; (d) Cosme Velho station 'guide' offering to 'skip the line' for R$ 100 cash — no skip exists, you'll just queue with everyone; (e) Paineiras shuttle 'fast-track upgrade R$ 80' (no upgrade tier exists); (f) 'private cable car booking R$ 600' at Urca base when the cable car is shared — no private option. For travellers: (1) book Christ the Redeemer ONLINE 1–2 weeks ahead via paineirascorcovado.com.br (Trem do Corcovado R$ 105–R$ 116 OR Paineiras Shuttle R$ 68) — NEVER via Viator / GetYourGuide / hotel concierge marked-up packages; (2) book Sugarloaf at bondinho.com.br at R$ 140; (3) REFUSE every 'skip-the-line', 'VIP tour', 'fast-track upgrade' upsell — none exists; (4) for travellers with mobility concerns, the Trem do Corcovado is much easier than Paineiras Shuttle (climb avoided); the Sugarloaf cable car is fully accessible; (5) optimal timing: Christ the Redeemer at 8 AM opening (avoids cloud + crowds); Sugarloaf at sunset (~5–6 PM Sept–Mar) for the legendary view; (6) bring layers — Corcovado summit is 10°C cooler than Copacabana; (7) AVOID Olafemi Tours per 2025 community warnings; reputable English-speaking operators: Tour Brazilis, Free Walker Tours, Carioca Tropical Tours, Rio By Cab.
scams.avoidance: Book Christ Redeemer ONLINE direct: paineirascorcovado.com.br R$ 105–R$ 116 Book Sugarloaf direct: bondinho.com.br R$ 140 REFUSE every 'skip-the-line' / 'VIP' / 'fast-track' upsell Optimal: Christ at 8 AM opening; Sugarloaf at sunset Reputable operators: Tour Brazilis, Free Walker Tours, Carioca Tropical, Rio By Cab
scams.location: Cosme Velho train station (Trem do Corcovado), Paineiras Shuttle Vans, Urca Sugarloaf cable-car base, Copacabana / Ipanema hotel-concierge tour desks

scams.name: Rio Favela Tour Unethical Operator & Fake-Charity 'Slum Safari' Scam
scams.description: Favela tours — Rocinha, Vidigal, Santa Marta — are Rio's most-controversial tourism category, and 2025 community discussion is increasingly critical of the unethical 'slum safari' operator ecosystem. Community reports from 2025 discuss the ethics of slum-safari tours, favela-tour experiences, a specific warning about a named operator titled 'DO NOT TOUR WITH OLAFEMI TOURS', and perspectives from local Brazilians. The 2025 issues: (a) 'safari-style' tours run by outsider operators with no community-benefit-share, treating residents as photo subjects without consent or revenue-share — ethics widely criticised; (b) operators charging US$ 50–US$ 150 per tourist for a 3-hour 'experience' with effectively zero direct compensation to the favela community; (c) safety variance — some operators take tourists into active-conflict zones during police operations or rival-faction periods (2025 Rio police operations have caused fatalities in tourist-area favelas); (d) 'photo with kids' upcharge demands (R$ 100+ for unsolicited child photos); (e) Olafemi Tours specifically named by 2025 community reports for problematic operator behaviour; (f) hostel tour-desk kickbacks pushing tourists toward unethical operators; (g) 'private favela house visit' upsells (R$ 200+) that are staged. For travellers seriously considering a favela visit: (1) the ethical case for 'favela tourism' is weak — most community organisations recommend NOT going as a tourist; the educational value can be obtained via documentaries (City of God, Wasteland) without the safety/consent issues; (2) IF you decide to visit, book ONLY community-led operators with verified resident-benefit revenue-share: Favela Inc (Rocinha resident-led), Tour Pelos Olhos da Rocinha (resident-led), Spirit Travel (community partnership); avoid Olafemi Tours per 2025 community warning; (3) NEVER book a favela tour during periods of active police operations — check Rio's official Polícia Militar updates BEFORE departure; (4) NEVER photograph residents (especially children) without explicit consent — Brazilian law and basic ethics prohibit; (5) refuse 'private house visit' upsells; (6) for cultural Rio tourism without favela-tour ethics issues, the Santa Teresa neighbourhood hilltop walk gives historic Rio vibes without exploiting working-class communities; (7) US Consulate Rio +55 21 3823 2000 if any tour goes wrong; (8) safer alternative: free walking tour of Lapa + Santa Teresa via Free Walker Tours (tip-based, well-reviewed).
scams.avoidance: Strongly consider NOT visiting — community ethics weak case for tourism If visiting, ONLY community-led: Favela Inc, Tour Pelos Olhos da Rocinha, Spirit Travel AVOID Olafemi Tours per 2025 community warning Check Polícia Militar updates BEFORE for active operations NEVER photograph residents (especially children) without consent
scams.location: Rocinha favela tours, Vidigal favela tours, Santa Marta favela tours, Cosme Velho tour-pickup vans, Lapa hostel tour-desk bookings

scams.name: Rio Carnaval & Réveillon Booking.com / Airbnb Cancel-and-Relist Fraud
scams.description: Rio Carnaval (4-day event around late Feb / early Mar) and Réveillon (NYE Copacabana, 2 million attendees) drive accommodation prices 4–8× normal — and a 2025 cancel-and-relist fraud ecosystem exploits the demand. A canonical 2024 community warning titled 'Warning! scam listings on booking.com for Carnaval' documents the Booking.com fraud. Other 2025 community reports document Carnaval-period booking patterns, Ipanema stays, and general Rio newbie tips. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) Booking.com / Airbnb 'phantom listings' — high-quality photos of properties that don't exist or are already booked; tourist pays in advance, arrives, finds no property; (b) confirmed-booking cancellation 30–60 days before Carnaval / Réveillon with re-listing at 3–5× the original price; (c) WhatsApp 'private Copacabana apartment for Réveillon US$ 800/night' demanding 100% upfront via PIX (Brazilian instant-bank transfer, irreversible) — apartment doesn't exist; (d) Sambódromo-adjacent 'VIP balcony view' Airbnb listings at US$ 5,000+/night that are actually rooms 500m away with no view; (e) on-arrival bait-and-switch from a beachfront unit to a 3-block-inland unit; (f) 'cleaning deposit US$ 300 cash on arrival' that never returns; (g) 'Carnaval VIP Sambódromo entry US$ 400' resold at 2–3× official Liesa box-office rate (real Setor 9 grandstand R$ 200–R$ 600). For travellers: (1) for Carnaval and Réveillon, BOOK 6–9 MONTHS AHEAD via Booking.com or established hotel chains (Hilton, Marriott, Belmond Copacabana Palace, Fasano, Pestana) — these have legal recourse against cancellation; AVOID Airbnb peak-season for Rio (cancel-and-relist pattern documented); (2) NEVER PIX or WhatsApp-bank-transfer to private 'apartment' sellers — irreversible Brazilian payment system; only platform-secure payment; (3) for Sambódromo Carnaval tickets, buy ONLY at the official Liesa box office (liesa.globo.com) — Setor 9 grandstand R$ 200–R$ 600 fair; refuse every 'VIP balcony view' resold above 2× official rate; (4) cross-reference any property name on Google Maps + Tripadvisor BEFORE booking — fake listings have no independent footprint; (5) on arrival, photograph property condition and any defects; refuse 'cleaning deposit cash on arrival' — request via platform only; (6) for Réveillon (NYE Copacabana), the safest accommodations are major Avenida Atlântica hotels — direct beachfront, no street-walk needed; (7) DEAT Tourist Police +55 21 2334 6802 for booking-fraud denuncia within 48 hours for chargeback documentation.
scams.avoidance: Book Carnaval / Réveillon 6–9 months ahead via hotel chains, NOT Airbnb Reputable: Hilton, Marriott, Belmond Copacabana Palace, Fasano, Pestana NEVER PIX/WhatsApp-bank-transfer to private 'apartment' sellers Sambódromo tickets ONLY from official Liesa: liesa.globo.com DEAT +55 21 2334 6802; chargeback denuncia within 48 hours
scams.location: Booking.com Rio Carnaval listings (Feb–Mar window), Réveillon (NYE) Copacabana hotel inventory, WhatsApp 'private apartment' Carnaval rentals, Airbnb Sambódromo-area listings
